log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Present a ranked reference list of the tallest buildings, with dimensions, location, completion year and explanatory comments.","tasks":["Identify a building by rank or name.","Compare heights and floor counts across buildings.","Find a building’s location and completion year.","Read comments for context and qualifications."],"relations":["Each row describes one building; rank, name and height are the main comparison path.","The m and ft columns are two units for the same height and belong under a shared header.","City and country jointly identify location; floor-count notes qualify the count."],"roles":["The first column is an unlabeled rank indicator; Name identifies the building.","Height has a grouped header and two unit subheaders; Floors, City, Country and Year are attributes.","Comments carry longer explanatory text and can dominate row height.","The two header rows establish the column hierarchy; body rows should remain easy to follow across the table."],"keep_whole":["Rank numbers, height values, floor counts, years and individual words.","The m and ft unit labels and the association of each floor count with its below-ground qualifier."],"may_wrap":["Building names at word boundaries.","Multiword cities and countries at word boundaries.","Floor-count qualifiers and comments at natural word boundaries."],"same_scale":["The two height columns should have nearly equal widths because they contain parallel measurements.","Rank and year should remain compact; name, location and comments need space according to their content rather than equal widths."],"h_vs_v":"The 719px limit leaves little room beyond the longest unbreakable units, so wrapping and taller rows are unavoidable. Extra width can reduce wrapping in names, floor qualifiers or comments, but giving it to one increases vertical density elsewhere."},"designs":[{"widths":[37,120,61,60,76,100,81,58,126],"strategy":"Favor building names while giving comments a modest share of the remaining space, supporting identification and rank lookup."},{"widths":[37,100,61,60,105,100,81,58,117],"strategy":"Give floor counts and their qualifiers more room, making comparisons of building dimensions easier at the cost of more wrapping in names and comments."},{"widths":[37,100,61,60,76,100,81,58,146],"strategy":"Concentrate the spare width in comments to improve continuous reading of explanatory notes, accepting narrower names and floor qualifiers."}]}
